children: SoftBank Group Corp. (SFTBY, Financials), the Japanese technology investment company, is reportedly planning $50 billion of investments in Malaysia as the country accelerates its push into artificial intelligence infrastructure.
Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said Masayoshi Son had identified potential investment locations in Kuching, Sarawak, and peninsular Malaysia.
The planned spending would focus on AI, emerging technologies and data centers. SoftBank has already taken an early step.
Earlier this month, the company signed a framework agreement with Grab and Petroleum Sarawak to explore AI computing services and digital infrastructure projects in Sarawak.
Malaysia is trying to position itself as a major regional AI and data-center hub by 2030.
The country recorded about 385.7 billion ringgit, or $94 billion, of data-center-related investments between 2021 and the first half of 2026.
Google, Amazon Web Services and Microsoft have also announced multibillion-dollar investments in the country.
For SoftBank, the proposed spending would deepen its exposure to the physical infrastructure behind the AI boom.
The next thing to watch is whether SoftBank formally commits the $50 billion and provides details on project timelines, ownership structures and expected returns.

title: SoftBank Plans $50 Billion Malaysia AI Push
